content: 1. On February 16, 2021, the World Health Organization (WHO) released an updated version of its consolidated WHO Guidelines for Malaria. For the first time, all current WHO recommendations for malaria prevention, case management, and elimination were compiled into a single, user-friendly online resource. These guidelines include evidence-based recommendations for malaria prevention (such as vector control and preventive chemotherapies) and case management (diagnosis and treatment). Recommendations for malaria elimination settings are still under development. Additionally, the guidelines provide links to supplementary resources, including guidance on strategic data use, surveillance, monitoring, evaluation, operational manuals, handbooks, frameworks, and a glossary of terms and definitions. 2. On July 13, 2021, updates were made to the vector control guidance within the malaria prevention section. A systematic review of the impact of larval habitat modification and manipulation on malaria revealed insufficient evidence to support a recommendation for these interventions. This assessment highlighted evidence gaps requiring further data generation. A conditional recommendation for house screening was developed based on a systematic review of housing modifications. Background information was added to explain how insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) provide protection to both individual users and the broader community, drawing on recent studies that explored the biological mechanisms of ITNs, particularly their community effect. Updates were also made to clarify that data from insecticide resistance assays should not be used to select between different pyrethroid products. Resource estimates for WHO-recommended interventions were included to inform local costing studies and guide the selection of cost-effective intervention packages. Areas where evidence gaps remain and further research is needed were also updated. 3. On February 18, 2022, WHO issued its first-ever recommendation for a malaria vaccine. This recommendation was based on a comprehensive evidence review of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine and advice from the Malaria Policy Advisory Group (MPAG) and the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) on Immunization, following a joint session held on October 6, 2021. 4. On March 31, 2022, revisions were made to the vector control guidance in the malaria prevention section. Updates included a revised conditional recommendation for the deployment of pyrethroid-PBO nets, based on a systematic review. A recommendation was also formulated for the use of pyrethroid-only long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) or pyrethroid-PBO nets, and a separate conditional recommendation was made for indoor residual spraying (IRS) in areas affected by humanitarian emergencies. The sections on insecticide selection for IRS were updated to provide more detail on the risks of using DDT and the importance of considering alternative insecticides. Additional details on resource considerations, costs, and cost-effectiveness for WHO-recommended interventions were added to inform local costing studies and guide intervention package selection. Updates were also made to identify evidence gaps and research needs for further revisions to malaria vector control guidance. 5. On June 13, 2022, updates were made to the recommendations for malaria chemoprevention. These included updates to recommendations for intermittent preventive treatment during pregnancy (IPTp), perennial malaria chemoprevention (PMC, previously referred to as intermittent preventive treatment in infants or IPTi), seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC), and new recommendations for intermittent preventive treatment in school-aged children (IPTsc), post-discharge malaria chemoprevention (PDMC), mass drug administration (MDA) for malaria burden and transmission reduction, and mass relapse prevention. This version also introduced the first WHO recommendations for interventions in the final phase of malaria elimination and prevention of re-establishment. These recommendations were based on evidence reviews of mass testing and treatment, targeted testing and treatment, targeted testing and treatment at points of entry, reactive drug administration, reactive case detection and treatment, and reactive indoor residual spraying, as developed by a Guidelines Development Group (GDG) in August, November, and December 2021. 6. On November 25, 2022, updates were made to the case management of malaria. These included the addition of new molecules for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria, optimization of dosage regimens for anti-relapse treatment, and updates on the use of antimalarial medicines in special risk populations, including pregnant women. 7. On March 14, 2023, WHO introduced new recommendations for two classes of insecticide-treated nets (ITNs): pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr and pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen ITNs. These recommendations were based on evidence of the epidemiological impact of these ITNs. Given the increasing complexity of prioritizing limited resources across different ITN products, WHO and its partners developed separate guidance on ITN prioritization under resource-constrained conditions. 8. On October 16, 2023, WHO revised its recommendations for the use of indoor residual spraying (IRS) to prevent malaria and issued a conditional recommendation against the use of topical repellents for malaria control at the community level. These updates were informed by recently updated systematic reviews and the outcomes of a technical consultation on comparative efficacy assessments, which reviewed data on the new insecticide broflanilide for IRS use. While the recommendations themselves remained unchanged, revised evidence profiles replaced older reviews, providing more detailed information on how the recommendations were formulated. Practical information on the two interventions was included, and broflanilide was added as an insecticide covered under the WHO IRS recommendation for malaria control.
